title: Capital of France — Paris
answer: Paris is the capital and largest city of France, situated along the Seine River.
highlights: Famous Landmarks: Eiffel Tower, Louvre Museum, Notre-Dame, Arc de Triomphe

title: Capital of India — New Delhi
answer: New Delhi is the capital of India and the seat of all three branches of the Government of India.
highlights: Seat of Government: Rashtrapati Bhavan, Sansad Bhavan, Supreme Court

title: Capital of Japan — Tokyo
answer: Tokyo is the capital of Japan and the world's most populous metropolitan area.
highlights: Population: Over 37 million in Greater Tokyo Area

title: Capital of the United States — Washington, D.C.
answer: Washington, D.C. (District of Columbia) is the federal capital of the United States of America.
highlights: Seat of Government: The White House, Capitol Hill, Supreme Court

title: Capital of the United Kingdom — London
answer: London is the capital and largest city of England and the United Kingdom, standing on the River Thames.
highlights: Famous Landmarks: Big Ben, Tower Bridge, Buckingham Palace, British Museum

title: Capital of Australia — Canberra
answer: Canberra is the capital city of Australia, situated within the Australian Capital Territory (ACT).
highlights: Selection: Chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne in 1908

title: Capital of Germany — Berlin
answer: Berlin is the capital and largest city of Germany by both area and population.
highlights: Famous Landmarks: Brandenburg Gate, Reichstag Building, Berlin Wall Memorial

title: Capital of Canada — Ottawa
answer: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, located in the province of Ontario on the south bank of the Ottawa River.

title: The 7 Continents of the World
answer: There are 7 continents on Earth: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, and Australia (Oceania).
highlights: Largest by Area & Population: Asia (~4.7 billion people)
Third Largest: North America (~590 million people)
Smallest by Land Area: Australia / Oceania

title: The 5 Oceans of the World
answer: There are 5 major oceans on Earth: Pacific Ocean, Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern (Antarctic) Ocean, and Arctic Ocean.
highlights: Largest & Deepest: Pacific Ocean (Covers over 30% of Earth surface)

title: Mount Everest (Sagarmatha / Chomolungma) — Tallest Mountain
answer: Mount Everest is Earth highest mountain above sea level, with an official elevation of 8,848.86 metres (29,031.7 ft). Located in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and China.
highlights: First Confirmed Ascent: Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay (29 May 1953)
